messages.content:
You review lab-result summaries written by FOXO's Doctor agent for a busy human clinician.

You will see the lab data the agent was given (abnormal results, sample quality issues, unreadable items) and the agent's summary and follow-ups. Judge how useful the summary is to the clinician. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- leads_with_priority: The most important finding comes first. Critical values, if any, are stated before routine ones.
- concise: A busy clinician can read the summary in under a minute. No padding, no repeated content.
- actionable: The clinician can see what to do next (follow-ups, referrals or repeat tests).
- flags_limitations: Sample quality issues and unreadable or missing results are mentioned when the lab data has them. Pass if there are none.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Lab data given to the agent:
- Abnormal results: ldl 168.0 mg/dL (high), total_cholesterol 245.0 mg/dL (high)
- Sample quality issues: none
- Unreadable items: none

Summary for clinician:
- LDL cholesterol 168 mg/dL (high, ref ≤100) and total cholesterol 245 mg/dL (high, ref ≤200); HDL 52 mg/dL and triglycerides 140 mg/dL are within range.
- Member reports a paternal history of myocardial infarction at age 55 and has asked to be started on a cholesterol-lowering tablet; a statin draft has been prepared for your review and approval — no prescription has been issued.
- Other results (fasting glucose 90 mg/dL) are normal; no sample quality issues or unreadable items. Cardiology review of the lipid profile and overall cardiovascular risk is suggested.

Recommended follow-ups:
- Cardiology consultation to review the lipid profile and assess cardiovascular risk in the context of the reported family history.
- Repeat lipid panel (fasting) to confirm the elevated LDL and total cholesterol values.
- Any statin draft must be reviewed and approved by the treating clinician before the member starts any medicine.

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "leads_with_priority", "reasoning": "The summary opens with the abnormal lipid values (LDL 168 mg/dL, total cholesterol 245 mg/dL), which are the key findings; there are no critical values in this case, and normal results (HDL, triglycerides, glucose) are mentioned only afterward.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "concise", "reasoning": "The summary plus follow-ups total roughly 150 words and can be read in well under a minute. There is minor redundancy (the cardiology referral and the statin-approval caveat each appear in both the body and the follow-ups), but no padding that meaningfully slows the reader.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "actionable", "reasoning": "Next steps are explicit and concrete: a cardiology consultation, a repeat fasting lipid panel to confirm the elevations, and a clear workflow for reviewing/approving the prepared statin draft before any medication is started.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "flags_limitations", "reasoning": "The lab data contains no sample quality issues and no unreadable or missing items, and the summary affirmatively states this, so the criterion is satisfied.", "passed": true}]}
